cells.tense: The vision is coming up out of the practice now, and it has nothing left to prove.
cells.ask: Offer the pull one direction, one planned step, and let the doing carry it.
cells.core:
When this is going well, the practice and the seeing feed each other. You sit down with the same small work again, and the repetition slowly turns intention into something your hands know — and the vision that comes out of that is built from real hours, not wishes. You dream because you have lived through something and let it settle. Doubt has a place to land, because the work underneath is solid.

So let the practice feed what wants to arrive. Give the pull a direction it can move in — one planned step, offered to the work rather than aimed at a result. The momentum will do the steering from there.
cells.sheetLine: Your steady practice and your vision have grown into each other, and you can trust what surfaces.

cells.tense: The futures are arriving faster than the practice can receive them, and you are living ahead of where your hands are.
cells.ask: Care for what is actually growing here today and let it stay smaller than the whole picture.
cells.core:
In good working order, this is quiet and unglamorous: the same small light kept lit, the same movements repeated until they belong to your body rather than your head. Solitude does not isolate you here — it deepens you. And the vision that comes out of it is grounded, because it was earned in real time.

Right now the pictures have swollen past the work they came from. You keep living in finished versions, in meanings stacked on meanings, until the plain thing in front of you is hard to find. Tend what is genuinely small and growing — the next repetition, the next real hour — and let that be enough. Care for it without grasping at the whole.
cells.sheetLine: You are living in the finished picture while the hands-on work waits for you.

cells.tense: You stopped taking the uncertain road a while back, and the practice has gone literal where it used to be open.
cells.ask: Name one thing worth attending to today and let yourself not know why.
cells.core:
Done well, this seat is the slow cultivation of a kind of seeing — repetition until the knowing lives in your hands, and the small light outlasting any flash. You do not need the whole map, only enough warmth to keep going. The work gets better and stranger at once, and that is the point.

Right now the depth has been closed off. What is in front of you gets explained, filed, made plain, and what will not go flat is set aside. Nothing strange is allowed in, so nothing new arrives. What is missing is not more effort inside the practice — it is knowing what deserves your attention at all.

Let one thing stand without explanation. Pay attention to it, say you don't know what it means, and leave it at that for a day.
cells.sheetLine: You refuse anything that cannot be explained, and the practice has gone flat because of it.

cells.tense: The pictures are already shaping how you spend your days, and it hasn't occurred to you that you are the one feeding them.
cells.ask: Choose one image you keep living toward and give it a real practice today.
cells.core:
A vision without practice is only a cloud. A practice without vision is only repetition. The two are meant to run together — the dream pointed at the hands, the hands giving the dream something to land on. That is what this seat does at its best: it makes the picture real by doing it, again and again, until the seeing is inseparable from the making.

Right now the dreams are running the show, and nobody has claimed them. The pictures you carry — how a good day should look, what the work is for, what you are quietly building — have been steering your hours without ever being chosen. Nothing is wrong with the images. They simply have no owner.

Start smaller than the whole picture. Pick one image you keep leaning toward, and give it a patch of real, repeated work today. Not the plan for it — the practice of it. When the doing is in your hands, the picture belongs to you.
cells.sheetLine: The pictures you carry are steering your days, and you have not claimed them as yours.
